biggestGap: Shoulder girdle is bolted on, not grown: the neck drops into a flat horizontal shoulder bar and the deltoid sits as a separate sphere sealed off by an ink ring, with vertical ribcage sides and no lat flare beneath the arm. In the WoW grunt and the Valheim player the trapezius sweeps neck-to-shoulder and the lat flares out under the armpit, so shoulder mass IS body mass. Ours reads as armor plus a ball joint on all three figures, worst on the orc.
notes:
HUMAN vs Valheim player / WoW grunt: reference wins, but the round-21 'stick figure wearing a helmet' charge is largely answered - pauldrons, pec/ab value bands, a bicep bulge and real thigh-top mass now give a shoulder-over-pelvis read, and the silhouette panel is no longer a coat hanger. It still loses because the mass is worn, not built: strip the pauldrons and the deltoid is a pale straight tube, the ribcage has no lat flare, and the forearm ends in a mitten sealed by a hard ink ring at the wrist. Verdict on the round-21 question: the human has closed most of the gap on the dwarf and is no longer the outlier - the orc is.

ORC vs WoW grunt: reference wins by a wide margin and this is now the weakest figure. The deltoids read as two spheres stuck onto a slab torso with an ink ring at each seam, there is no neck, the waist never narrows against the hips, and the legs are parallel tubes with no knee event; the face close-up is a bald olive egg with painted-on brow slabs, two flat white tusk cards, no nose, no ears and no jaw mass, where the grunt carries brow, jaw, ears, hair and beard.

DWARF vs Valheim greydwarf brute / WoW grunt: credible tie, and the strongest of the three - broad helmeted chest over short braced legs, a real wide-set stance, arms that taper from a thick upper arm to a smaller forearm, and the only hand on the sheet that reads thumb-plus-four-fingers near panel distance (the free fist; the sword grip hand is still a knot). It loses only on gear layering and material variety, where the grunt stacks belts, fur cuffs and boot bands.

HANDS: free fists read as mitts with grooves at 3x but collapse to pale lozenges at panel distance on human and orc; every grip hand is a lumpy clump around the tang, with the human's thumb reading as an orange proboscis. FEET (front panel): all three wear toe-less potato blobs - no toe box, no ankle, no left/right difference, no toe splay, and the shin enters the boot through an ink ring. GEAR: pauldrons seat well and have real thickness on human and dwarf; the orc wears none and has nothing to hide behind.

HARNESS: no broken panels. The pale ghost column at the right of the side panels is the known scale figure. Minor framing miss on all three sheets: the 'top' panel figure sits low and left of its cell instead of centered, so the top-down camera does not appear to be aiming at the model root.
